question: What three main components make up Moshi's architecture?
answer: The three main components of Moshi's architecture are a bespoke text language model backbone (Helium), a neural audio codec with residual vector quantization and distilled semantic knowledge (Mimi), and the streaming, hierarchical generation of semantic and acoustic tokens for both the user and Moshi, including time-aligned text tokens for Moshi when using Inner Monologue [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6].

question: What compression target N₀ did the one-stage H-Net language-model experiment use?
